newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mosenergo sees 50 pct rate rise on 21 pct of sales.
newsitem.headline: Mosenergo sees 50 pct rate rise on 21 pct of sales.

text.p: Russian utility Mosenergo expects to raise rates by 50 percent on sales on the federal wholesale market, presently 21 percent of Mosenergo capacity sales, a spokesman for its planning department said on Friday.

Alexander Rayev did not say when the change was likely to go into effect but said that sales on the market should rise to 160 roubles per kilowatt-hour from 109 roubles, according to Mosenergo's calculations.

The Federal Energy Commission itself will name the new rate for Mosenergo, and no date for the commission's next meeting has been scheduled, but Rayev said that the Moscow utility had discussed its calculations with commission employees.

A government order which came into effect February 13 allows utilies which overproduce for their own region's needs to include expenses related to maintaining and expanding generating capacity into their prices on the federal wholesale market.
"By our calculation, the tariffs on electricity should rise to one and a half times the current level, which will guarantee us 160 roubles/kilowatt-hour," he said.

Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov said earlier this week that he intended to approach the federal Antimonopoly Committee about the current low price at which Mosenergo is forced to sell electricity on the federal wholesale market.
Luzhkov said that Mosenergo's cost for supplying electricity to the federal market was 188 roubles/kilowatt-hour.
OAO Energetiki i Elektrifikatsii Mosenergo generated 73.1 billion kilowatt-hours in 1996 and sells 21 percent of its output on the federal wholesale market, Rayev said.
